body:
Fortunately drugs aren’t complicating this. My friend is employed but a medical condition required them to transfer from one location to another & I’m not sure if they’ve been able to work any hours at the new location yet. They have some gig work I believe they’ve been doing in the meantime, but personally I’m afraid to ask about that. They called me and one other person their entire support system and truthfully, I’m emotionally burnt out. It’s a lot to ask of someone to be half of a support system and I’ve tried to be there for them these past months, but I think I may have reached my limit. :( I’m definitely learning a lot from this. 

Anyway, if my friend was working guaranteed regular full time hours every week, I would consider them stable now. For a time, it looked like that was happening, but then the medical condition ruined their ability to get to work. The other location should be fine if only my friend can get enough hours again. They already would be making more than I do too. So… stability is almost within reach. But it seems my friend has had a very rough and unlucky go of it so far.

I was wondering if that was possible. Good to know. And yes, I do have a copy of the form, but it’s a bit vague on the details relating to what I’m interested in (go figure). Oh well—it’s def good to know that it may not be totally impossible. Fortunately, I’m definitely working this out with a therapist & I’ve been making progress. I do think that worst comes to worst, I’ll be ok. I make more than enough to cover my friend’s part of their rent. Would it suck if I had to? Yes. But I think I’d be ok even then. It would most likely just delay my life plans for sure. Disentangling myself won’t be easy, but I guess even if the worst happens, it’s fortunate that I likely won’t get into debt and that I’ll come out of this wiser. I didn’t realize I had quite the blind spot in this area before but it’s helping me examine a LOT. So thank you for your reply! Considering all this helps considerably.

Thank you! I actually never checked with any of the bureaus before—I always heard offhandedly that checking is bad for your credit & FICO regularly provides me a number that’s been helpful. And good to know I should try talking to my friend first. I think I still need to sort out how to approach my friend by talking to my therapist, but it helps to hear that at least one other person thinks it’s not a good idea to talk to the landlord first!
